title: refactor(cli): optimize slash command resolution parsing with pre-computed map

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue clearly identifies a performance bottleneck and an existing TODO comment in packages/cli/src/utils/commands.ts regarding two-pass linear search during slash command resolution, offering a clear and actionable O(1) map lookup refactoring plan.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The refactoring is a localized logic change within packages/cli/src/utils/commands.ts and packages/cli/src/services/CommandService.ts to build and query a pre-computed command lookup map, supported by existing unit tests.

summary.problem: Slash command resolution in parseSlashCommand performs a two-pass linear search over commands and their aliases for each path segment.
summary.root_cause: Commands and subcommands are searched sequentially via Array.prototype.find twice per path segment—first for primary names and then for alternate names.
summary.context: A TODO comment in packages/cli/src/utils/commands.ts highlights this exact optimization opportunity, suggesting a pre-computed lookup map in CommandService.ts.

steps: Create a helper or map structure to index command names and altNames to their corresponding SlashCommand objects.
Refactor parseSlashCommand in packages/cli/src/utils/commands.ts to perform single O(1) map lookups instead of two-pass find searches.
Expose or pre-compute the lookup map in CommandService.ts during command loading and conflict resolution.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Command and subcommand resolution continues to function identically for primary names, aliases, subcommands, arguments, and backtracking, but with O(1) lookup efficiency.
verification_steps: Run npx vitest run packages/cli/src/utils/commands.test.ts to verify all command parsing tests pass.
Add unit test cases verifying primary name and alias lookup map resolution.
